REQUIREMENTS_ANALYSIS.EFFECTIVE_SPECIFICATION: Only ISSUE32 defines the target contract. Previous specifications are available in immutable Git history and Issue #25 approval discussions; they are not part of these active XML artifacts. No /v1, /v2, Bearer, legacy-client support or data migration.

ISSUE32_REQUIREMENTS_REVISION.SCOPE: Target-only correction. Historical approved clauses and approval records remain as evidence of prior decisions; incompatible historical API paths are not the target contract. No production implementation authorized.
ISSUE32_REQUIREMENTS_REVISION.GOAL: One unified direct/group conversation service exposed solely through the unversioned /conversations HTTP resource tree, authenticated exclusively with BFE Drive Internal Auth validated DPoP-bound sessions.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: All target conversation HTTP operations use /conversations and its unversioned descendants. /v1 and /v2 are not target HTTP APIs. Existing /v2 domain behavior is the implementation migration baseline, not a second API.

Every protected target HTTP request requires DPoP proof bound to the validated BFE Drive session through existing Internal Auth; plain Bearer is not an accepted authentication scheme. WebSocket authentication and subscriptions preserve required independent membership verification and revocation rules.
Direct and group conversations share one conversation identity, message stream, authorization model and history semantics, retaining type-specific membership and ownership rules.

Retain all functional direct/group conversation behavior, permissions, message/document handling and idempotency from the working /v2 implementation. No legacy-client support, production-data inventory or migration is in scope; destructive removal of populated legacy tables is not authorized.

A 1:1 conversation is created by authenticated account UUID and distinct peer UUID. Self-direct is rejected. Creation for the same unordered pair is unique and concurrency-safe. Personal hide affects only caller visibility, never peer access, messages or direct identity.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: Verify authorized success, unauthorized rejection, concurrency or boundary behavior for direct without changes to legacy clients or production data.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: Authenticated user creates named group with owner and selected account UUIDs. Maximum 100 members including owner. Creator is owner. Group supports rename, invited-member changes, role management and departure. A member may leave. The owner must transfer ownership to another current group member before leaving; if there is no other current member, the last owner cannot leave. Exactly one owner must remain after each successful operation.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: Verify authorized success, unauthorized rejection, concurrency or boundary behavior for group without changes to legacy clients or production data.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: Owner may manage group and appoint or dismiss admins, while preserving exactly one owner; admin can only perform explicitly allowed membership or rename operations, cannot remove owner/other admin, appoint admins or transfer ownership; member cannot administer group. BFE Drive ADMIN status does not grant Chat membership or management.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: Verify authorized success, unauthorized rejection, concurrency or boundary behavior for roles without changes to legacy clients or production data.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: Every membership addition/removal creates an auditable bounded visibility interval. Read and message delivery are permitted only for messages within caller intervals. On rejoin, messages from the gap stay hidden. Removal immediately blocks subsequent protected operations and active WebSocket subscriptions. Membership mutations and send/delivery authorization have a defined atomic ordering.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: Verify authorized success, unauthorized rejection, concurrency or boundary behavior for membership without changes to legacy clients or production data.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: Each conversation has one stable monotonic conversation-scoped message order and cursor pagination, default 50 and max 100 messages per page. Every history query filters by authenticated viewer membership intervals. The same visibility rule applies to reconnect and historical catch-up.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: Verify authorized success, unauthorized rejection, concurrency or boundary behavior for history without changes to legacy clients or production data.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: Only authenticated current members send messages; sender identity is never supplied by a trusted client field. Text maximum 16384 UTF-8 bytes, request JSON maximum 65536 bytes. Idempotency key replay returns original result for identical content and 409 Conflict for different content; concurrency cannot create duplicates.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: Verify authorized success, unauthorized rejection, concurrency or boundary behavior for message without changes to legacy clients or production data.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: Optional message context holds document ID and title; preserve both in message history and events. Chat neither copies document content nor grants any BFE Drive document rights. Document access is independently checked by BFE Drive.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: Verify authorized success, unauthorized rejection, concurrency or boundary behavior for document without changes to legacy clients or production data.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: Centrifuge publishes persisted messages only to currently authorized members. Revalidate authorized subscriptions and revocation even for established sockets. Reconnect recovers missed messages through persisted conversation history; multi-device membership and read states remain coherent.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: Verify authorized success, unauthorized rejection, concurrency or boundary behavior for realtime without changes to legacy clients or production data.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: Read marker is monotonically increasing per account and conversation and shared across devices. Unread counts include only authorized messages sent by other users. One member cannot advance another member read marker.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: Verify authorized success, unauthorized rejection, concurrency or boundary behavior for read without changes to legacy clients or production data.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: All Chat-specific conversation state and ACLs are within bfe_chat. BFE Drive sessions are validated through existing Internal Auth UDS; account UUID alone grants no Chat authorization. Reject out-of-scope access without leaking data.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: Verify authorized success, unauthorized rejection, concurrency or boundary behavior for isolation without changes to legacy clients or production data.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: Group names limited to 256 UTF-8 bytes; no more than 100 group members; JSON body max 65536 bytes; message text max 16384 UTF-8 bytes; history page max 100. Reject invalid input before changes or publications.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: Verify authorized success, unauthorized rejection, concurrency or boundary behavior for limits without changes to legacy clients or production data.

DPoP-bound authorized requests succeed; Bearer-only, missing/replayed/misbound proofs fail without side effects.

Target-only functional checks confirm direct/group message and document handling, membership, access restrictions, ordering and idempotency. No legacy-client or production-data validation is required.

ISSUE36_REQUIREMENTS_REVISION.SCOPE: Propose replacing Centrifuge with ntfy as the chat realtime notification transport. This revision is not effective until Human Approval. The approved ISSUE32 baseline remains effective in the meantime. This proposal authorizes no code implementation, production configuration change, deployment, or database operation.
ISSUE36_REQUIREMENTS_REVISION.PROJECT_GOAL: Replace Centrifuge with ntfy for chat realtime notifications while preserving backend-authoritative message history, membership authorization, sender exclusion, privacy, and production safeguards.
ISSUE36_REQUIREMENTS_REVISION.ACTOR: Authenticated current conversation member other than the sender

USE_CASE.ACTION: Commits a chat message through the backend
USE_CASE.GOAL: Notify other currently authorized members that backend history may have changed without disclosing message or document data through ntfy

REQUIREMENT.RULE: ntfy replaces Centrifuge as the sole target realtime notification transport. The target architecture must not retain Centrifuge as a parallel or fallback chat realtime transport. ntfy transports wake-up notifications only; it is not the source of truth for messages, ordering, membership, or authorization.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: After separately authorized implementation, the runtime and dependency inventory shows ntfy as the realtime notification transport and no Centrifuge runtime path.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: The backend remains authoritative for committed messages, conversation history, ordering, membership intervals, roles, authorization, and read visibility. Receiving an ntfy event never grants access to a conversation or message. Clients obtain message data only through authenticated backend operations that re-check current authorization and history visibility.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: A notification alone cannot read protected data; backend authorization rejects non-members, removed members, and requests outside the caller's permitted membership interval.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: A notification may be published only after the corresponding message is durably committed. Notify only currently authorized conversation members other than the sender. Replaying an idempotent message request must not create another notification. Recipient eligibility and membership epoch must be revalidated before publication; stale or revoked membership epochs must not authorize new delivery.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: Tests prove that uncommitted messages produce no notification, the sender receives no notification for their own message, authorized other members can be notified, removed members cannot be newly notified, and an idempotent replay does not publish again.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: Each active membership epoch uses a distinct opaque, unpredictable ntfy topic. Topic names must not encode account IDs, conversation IDs, message IDs, document identifiers, titles, or content. ntfy access control is enabled with default-deny behavior and no anonymous topic access. Only the backend publisher may publish, and only the corresponding currently authorized member may subscribe. Removal revokes access to the old epoch; rejoining creates a new epoch and topic. Topic secrecy alone is not an authorization mechanism.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: Unauthenticated access, cross-member topic access, publishing by clients, and subscription to a revoked epoch are denied. Rejoining does not restore access to the previous epoch topic.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: The application-supplied ntfy message body contains exactly the minimal wake-up envelope fields version (integer) and wakeToken (opaque random identifier). The wakeToken must not encode or expose account, conversation, message, or document identifiers. No message text, sender identity, document ID, document title, document content, URLs, attachments, notification title, tags, actions, or other application data may be supplied in the ntfy message or metadata. Authentication credentials and wake tokens must not be written to application logs.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: Capture the complete application-supplied publish request and verify that the body has only version and wakeToken and that no protected content or identifying application metadata is present in the topic, request metadata, or application logs.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: Document ID and title may remain in authorized backend message history and backend events where required by the message contract. Neither document ID nor title, document contents, nor document access credentials may be included in ntfy messages or notification metadata. Chat notifications do not grant BFE Drive document access; document authorization remains independently enforced by BFE Drive.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: A message with document context retains its authorized backend history fields while captured ntfy requests and notification metadata contain no document identifier, title, contents, link, or access credential.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: ntfy delivery is a wake-up signal and is not the durable message stream. Clients recover missed messages, ordering, and visibility by querying backend history using the approved cursor contract. Missing, duplicated, delayed, or out-of-order ntfy notifications must not cause message loss, duplicate durable messages, ordering changes, or access to history outside the caller's authorized membership intervals.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: Scenarios with lost, duplicated, delayed, and reordered notifications recover the same authorized backend history in the same stable order without duplicate message creation or visibility gaps being exposed.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: ntfy unavailability, publish errors, or timeouts must not roll back or erase a durably committed message. Preserve explicit notification-attempt outcomes and the existing protection against blind retries after an ambiguous publish outcome. Notification delivery failure must not bypass backend authorization or change message history.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: When ntfy is unavailable or a publish outcome is ambiguous, the committed message remains readable to authorized members, notification outcomes are recorded according to the approved contract, and no unsafe retry or duplicate protected payload is emitted.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: This requirements proposal authorizes no implementation, dependency change, production configuration change, database migration, merge to the effective baseline, or deployment. Those actions remain gated on Human Approval of this revision and approval of all dependent GRACE artifacts and checks.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: No production or runtime artifact changes are included in this requirements-only revision; implementation remains blocked until all required GRACE approvals are recorded.

ISSUE36_REQUIREMENTS_REVISION.INVARIANT: Only the backend's committed state and authorization checks determine message visibility and access.
The sender is never an ntfy recipient for their own message.
ntfy application payload and metadata contain no message or document content and no identifying application fields beyond the approved opaque wake-up envelope.
A revoked membership epoch cannot authorize new topic subscriptions or backend history access; a later membership uses a fresh epoch.
ntfy failure cannot invalidate or remove a committed backend message.

BUSINESS_PROCESS.STEP: A client submits a message to the authenticated backend.
The backend validates membership and authorization and durably commits the message using the existing message contract.
The backend identifies current authorized recipients other than the sender and revalidates their membership epochs.
The backend publishes only the approved opaque wake-up envelope to each eligible recipient's protected ntfy topic.
A recipient treats the notification only as a wake-up signal and fetches authorized history from the backend.
On removal or rejoin, the old membership epoch loses authorization and the new epoch receives a distinct topic.
